chunks: Al-Husayn ibn ʿUbayd Allah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Jaʿfar, from his father, that ʿAli عليه السلام said:

The milk of a baby girl and her urine are such that the garment is washed from them before she begins to eat, because her milk comes out from her mother’s bladder. And the milk of a baby boy—the garment is not washed from it, nor from his urine, before he begins to eat, because the milk of the baby boy comes out from the upper arms and the shoulders.

key_terms.لَبَنُ: milk; here, the milk associated with an infant

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on washing clothes affected by the urine of an infant boy or girl before they begin eating?
ai.summary: This hadith presents a legal ruling concerning ritual purity related to the urine and milk of infant girls and boys before they begin eating food. It attributes a distinction in washing garments to the source of the milk as described in the narration.
